newsitem.title: USA: BPA says power demand, flow limits cut surplus.
newsitem.headline: BPA says power demand, flow limits cut surplus.

text.p: An expected seasonal increase in Northwest electricity demand along with flow constraints linked to fish spawning have cut surplus power volumes, the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Thursday.
"(Earlier this week) we only had a very small surplus and we sold everything we had," said a BPA marketing source.
He noted temperatures in the Pacific Northwest are forecast to fall back into seasonally normal ranges from recent above-normal levels, in turn pushing up demand.
Furthermore, flows on the Columbia River's hydroelectric dam system remain constrained by the need to keep daytime flows at levels low enough to be maintained until late spring.
"This limits flow at (Grand) Coulee," said the BPA source. The flow limits are scheduled to expire just before the November 28 Thanksgiving Day holiday.
Reservoirs in the region are also being managed to attain year-end storage targets, some of which are also related to fish migration.
But BPA does not anticipate a big change in surplus volumes after the end of the year.
"Even if we have the same (above normal) runoff volume forecasts in January that we had this year, we are not seeing the same warm, rainy pattern," that occured late last year, the BPA source said.

In addition, talks are still underway with Canadian fish and wildlife authorites about joint river operations which could impact flows on the Columbia system early next year. The headwaters of some Columbia River tributaries are in British Columbia.
Bonneville is also seeking to sell as much surplus power as possible under forward block deals, regional sources said.
